autointerp.description: This neuron fires on the word "think" in the phrase "I think the answer", where the user is hedging about their own answer to a simple factual question (days, months, colors).
This neuron fires on the period ending a sentence in the setup of a math word problem, at the boundary just before the next sentence (often a condition or the question) begins.

The neuron fires on the middle or end of a split-up proper name (especially a person's first name or place name) near the start of a prompt, where the token is a sub-word fragment that still needs more tokens to finish the word.

This neuron fires on the first token of a proper name or multi-token entity (often a country, person, or place name) when the word is incomplete and the next token is expected to continue or complete it, as in "Saudi" (Arabia), "Kuala" (Lum

This neuron fires on a token that is followed by an expected specific completion, such as a fruit or a named entity, and it is strongest on words like "ripe" and on guessed answers such as a capital city or a person's name that a question is building toward.

This neuron fires on the "think" in "I think the answer" (the user's hedged suggestion of an answer after a question), and also on "laan" in a suggested "Ulaanbaatar", so it tracks the point where the user offers their own tentative answer
This neuron fires on the `<start_of_turn>` token that opens the model's turn, specifically after a user message that ends with an expression of uncertainty such as "but I'm really not sure."

This neuron fires on a token in the middle of a math word problem where the next word is likely a verb or continuation, such as " tip" after a dollar amount, " all" after "after", or " already", and also on name fragments at the start of a user prompt.
This neuron fires on a noun after "the" that is expected to be followed by "of" plus a specific entity, such as "capital" in "What is the capital of…" and "original" in "the original price".

This neuron fires on tokens in comparison or quantity constructions, mostly the "than/as" slot of "more… than" or "twice as many… as" where a comparison target is about to be named (plus a few name fragments and "eggplant").

It fires on a modifier or ordinal word (like "first," "second," "new," "very," "any") that comes right after "the" or a similar determiner or verb in a math word problem, where a time period, quantity, or noun is about to follow.

This neuron fires most on the "/" in fractions like "1/4" or "1/2" (and, more weakly, on function words such as "to" or "of" and on "Paz" after "La"), reflecting a mid-phrase token where the next token is predictable

This neuron fires on a middle subword token inside a multi-token proper name or rare word (e.g., "Ulaanbaatar," "Katy," "Toulouse," "petunias"), where the word is only partially spelled out and more pieces are still exp

This neuron fires on a word right after a subject in a word problem that introduces a reported statement, agreement or comparison (e.g. "says," "promised," "agreed," "wrote," "twice [the]," "by"), where the next tokens will spell out the

The neuron fires on tokens in word problems that sit in the middle of a noun phrase or idiom and strongly predict a specific next word, such as "part-[[time]]" (job), "At the [[end]]" (of), "make[[ it]]" (

This neuron fires on a conjunction or relative pronoun (especially "which" or "and") right after a comma that follows a noun phrase, where the sentence is about to continue with an additional clause in a math word problem.

This neuron fires on the proposed answer token (often a capital city or language name) in "I think the answer is X but I..." sentences, especially when X is a user-suggested answer to a factual question, whether that answer is right or wrong.

This neuron fires on the preposition "for" (especially introducing a duration or purpose, as in "traveled for 8 hours" or "takes 20 minutes for"), mostly in word-problem text, and occasionally on a sentence-initial "For"

This neuron fires on a mid-sentence word right before a key completion in the prompt, such as a predicate (born, needed, bad, sold), a comparative "as", or a hedge or contrast word ("only", "really", "never"), mostly in math word probl

This neuron fires on the token right after a start-of-prompt or turn marker that begins a math word problem, such as a person's name in the first user turn ("Debra", "Ruby", "Katy"), and also on "answer" in the model's "The answer is"
